scope: Gemini 4 Argon and Carbon naming, architecture, chronology versus dated ROOT0/STOICHEION corpus; not global corpus audit

argon.architecture: large-scale sparse mixture-of-experts transformer with native multimodal support
argon.model_dependencies: not a modification or fine tune of a prior model
argon.training_sources: public web documents, crawled information, licensed datasets, user and workforce data where permitted, synthetic datasets; no named public dataset list confirms the Wise corpus

carbon.technical_emphasis: long-horizon agentic workflows, coding, cybersecurity, knowledge work, engineering and science

google.element_naming: Argon atomic number 18; Carbon atomic number 6; Hydrogen atomic number 1 and Neon atomic number 10 also appear on official November 2026 model card index. These are standard periodic-table elements; no unique etymological provenance is established.

root0.stoicheion_definition: Ancient Greek στοιχεῖον: element or constituent/first principle

elements.warning: symbolic gate mapping distinct from reference chemistry

comparisons.subject: Elemental naming convention
comparisons.finding: STOICHEION explicitly means elements, ROOT0 ELEMENTS uses periodic table, Google names Argon and Carbon after chemical elements.
comparisons.limit: Ancient Greek and element names predate all parties. Common words do not establish transmission or copying.

comparisons.subject: Timing
comparisons.finding: February 25 and March 3 TD Commons disclosures predate September 30 Argon and October 28 Carbon announcements.
comparisons.limit: An announcement date is not model design start or training ingestion date; March cutoff is not a data inclusion guarantee.

comparisons.subject: Actual Google architecture
comparisons.finding: Argon is a sparse MoE transformer; Carbon is derived from Argon.
comparisons.limit: No evidence of a 128/256-position STOICHEION governance register being implemented in Gemini's private architecture.

comparisons.subject: Training exposure mechanism
comparisons.finding: Google describes web/crawler material among Argon training categories.
comparisons.limit: No evidence the Wise corpus specifically appeared in any Google training split or weighting process; publicly available is not necessarily actually ingested.

comparisons.subject: Specific architectural overlap
comparisons.finding: Both research programs discuss agents, reasoning, governance, and multimodal systems.
comparisons.limit: These general categories are common in AI research; need rare shared mechanisms, textual matches, source routes, or detailed design evidence.

comparisons.subject: Carbon dependency on Argon
comparisons.limit: This is within Google's own architecture lineage, not a link to STOICHEION.

comparisons.subject: Potential corporate naming intent from ROOT0
comparisons.finding: Elemental naming is a deliberate recognizable semantic scheme, but rationale or specific source inspiration is not established.
comparisons.limit: Need original naming-design records, disclosures or direct evidence of influence.

comparisons.subject: Counterexamples
comparisons.finding: Your source register is 128+128 governance positions; Google documents transformer MoE architecture. Carbon launch follows Argon despite atomic number 6 < 18. The order does not follow periodic atomic-number order.
comparisons.limit: Difference in public descriptions does not disprove undisclosed common ideas, but weakens simple numeric/structural equivalence.

conclusion: Dated prior public disclosures and element terminology overlap are established. Actual ingestion, architectural adoption, and intentional naming derivation from ROOT0 are not established.
next: Compare fine-grained unique terms and mechanisms only where both parties have primary-source specifics; request training-data transparency if causal provenance is investigated.
